title: NASA's $600 Million Plan to Build a Moon Neighborhood!
summary:
Have you ever dreamed of living on the Moon? NASA is making that dream a big step closer! They just picked three companies to fly four new missions to the Moon in 2028. The goal? To build a permanent base where astronauts can live and work. It's like creating a tiny neighborhood on another world!

NASA is spending almost $600 million on these trips. That's a lot of money—imagine stacking 600 million one-dollar bills! The companies are Astrobotic, Firefly Aerospace, and Intuitive Machines. They'll each send a lander carrying science tools. Some of these tools are super cool. One is a set of four cameras called SCALPSS. It will take 3D videos of how rocket exhaust blows Moon dust around during landing. Why does that matter? Because when bigger spaceships land near each other, flying dust could be dangerous. Scientists want to understand it better.

Another tool is a Laser Retroreflector Array, or LRA. It's about the size of a cookie! This tiny device has eight special mirrors that bounce laser beams back to spaceships. It helps them know exactly where they are—like a GPS for the Moon. And it never needs batteries, so it can work forever as a permanent marker.

There's also a radiation monitor to keep future astronauts safe. Plus, NASA is thinking about sending a rover called PROMISE. It's a mix of the Mars rovers Perseverance and Curiosity, and it would hunt for useful resources like water ice.

All these missions are part of NASA's Moon Base Program. They want to learn how to live on the Moon so that one day, people can stay there for a long time. Who knows? Maybe you'll be one of them!
why_it_matters: If NASA builds a neighborhood on the Moon, one day you might visit it like a field trip, and studying Moon dust helps keep astronauts safe for future explorers.

keywords.explanation: A lander is a spacecraft that softly touches down on the surface of a moon or planet instead of crashing.
Exhaust is the hot, fast-moving gas that shoots out of a rocket engine when it burns fuel.
A Laser Retroreflector Array is a group of tiny mirrors that bounce laser beams straight back, like a GPS marker that never needs batteries.
SCALPSS is a set of four cameras that film 3D videos of how rocket exhaust kicks up Moon dust during landing.
Radiation is invisible high-energy waves or tiny bits that can be dangerous to living things in large amounts.
Water ice is frozen water, like ice cubes, but on the Moon it is mixed into the soil or hidden in cold, dark craters.

background_read: NASA’s Apollo program sent humans to the Moon for the first time in 1969, but no one has walked on the Moon since 1972.
Now NASA’s Artemis program plans to return astronauts and build a long-term base on the Moon.
The three companies chosen—Astrobotic, Firefly Aerospace, and Intuitive Machines—are private spacecraft builders helping NASA deliver science gear.
Article_Structure: WHO: NASA and three private companies—Astrobotic, Firefly Aerospace, and Intuitive Machines.
WHAT: Sending four new missions in 2028 to land scientific tools and build a permanent Moon base.
WHY: To learn how to live and work on the Moon so humans can stay for long periods.

perspectives.description: Advocates say this is a thrilling step toward humans becoming a space-faring species, opening up new scientific discoveries and inspiring kids worldwide.
Critics argue that nearly $600 million could be used to solve problems on Earth, like hunger, disease, and climate change, instead of building a Moon base.
Scientists see these missions as necessary to test technologies for longer stays, but they acknowledge risks like Moon dust damaging equipment and the need for careful planning.
